item: The session-forensics byte room is measured with the real code: three launcher stderr sessions instead of four, counts saturating at "999999+", died_into_phase reasons as short codes the readers map back to words
summary: WAL measured the RC2 members at 2,521 to 2,713 B against 2,415 B; the pin test summed typed figures and could not fail. launcher_stderr is 319 B per session at worst (not 250; the largest shape is a 120-character macOS line beside lines_cut, every count saturated and a five-digit rejected_lines) so it now shows the previous session and 2 earlier unclean ends (it was 3); a count of 999,999 or more is written as the string "999999+" (never an exact-looking number; it protects the byte budget); died_into_phase reasons are no peaks, no phase, no phase start, clock moved, and the readers (render_text, the triage) map each back to its former words. tests/test_session_forensics_budget.py builds every member in its worst case with the real code and sums them with WAL's crashing_thread_kind 440: 2,373 B of 2,415 B, 42 B left unspent (WAL re-measured the same figure independently); red if any member grows (mutations: 4 rows, no count cap, the plain cap, the long reason, a 200 character share). Losses: the oldest of the earlier ends loses its stderr lines (not its signal, status or trace); a stderr count past a million is not exact; the stored died_into_phase reason says less (the readers restore the words).
